prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (call sign "Juniper"), 24/7 primary regional dispatch/coordination point: intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch, coordination across participating jurisdictions; turns emergencies into prioritized incidents under approved clinical/jurisdictional protocols; maintains shared picture of incidents, units, access constraints. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership and local policy; regional service coordinates agreed response.

Actors:
- Call Taker Mara: obtains incident details, confirms location, enters request.
- Triage Supervisor: assigns/confirms priority, directs cases to clinical review.
- Regional Medical Director: sets clinical triage policy and protocol limits.
- Dispatch personnel: must apply approved protocols, seek clinical guidance beyond delegated authority; consider travel time, restrictions, weather, closures for routes/ETAs.
- Shift Commander ("Sundial"): operational authority, surge priorities, escalates to jurisdictional leadership; must not override Regional Medical Director's clinical policy or Paramedic Crew's on-scene judgment.
- Radio Coordinator ("Mistral"): monitors Regional Radio Network; confirms channels and backup procedures at each shift start; radio checks of weak-signal coverage and equipment/network faults.
- Fleet Maintenance Cell ("Bluejay"): monitors vehicle availability, servicing, defects affecting zone coverage; produces Battery Swap Voucher (documents authorized battery replacement).
- Data Quality Officer: reviews dispatch records for completeness, consistency, information-handling compliance.
- Paramedic Crew: patient assessment/care; crews verify conditions before committing to constrained routes.
- Hospital Liaison Desk: receiving capacity/destination constraints.
- Emergency Department: receiving considerations via regional procedures.

Elements: Regional Radio Network; Ambulance Coordination Platform; Computer Aided Dispatch Console; Ambulance Unit 417; Riverside Trauma Center; North Gate Status Board (northern access/queue; produces North Approach Queue Snapshot for congestion view); South Gate Status Board (southern access incl. ambulance entry restrictions). Both boards checked at shift start and on reported access changes.

Response zones: defined by distance, road access, capacity; boundaries maintained with jurisdictions, reviewed on road/population/agreement changes; each zone has primary and alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center.

Readiness checks per available ambulance: staffing, comms, clinical supplies, fuel, vehicle condition, maintenance restrictions.

Items: emergency requests, incident details/location, priorities, unit assignments, resource status, receiving capacity, access status, North Approach Queue Snapshot, Battery Swap Voucher, dispatch records.

New part:
S044: The Ambulance Coordination Platform provides a shared operational view of zone coverage and unit availability.
S045: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports dispatch work, while operational staff remain responsible for verifying that displayed information is current.
S046: The Shift Commander reviews readiness concerns that may require repositioning resources or adjusting local coverage plans.
S047: The Triage Supervisor coordinates clinical prioritization with dispatch operations when demand or access conditions change.
S048: The Paramedic Crew reports new access barriers and vehicle readiness concerns through established communications procedures.
S049: The Regional Dispatch Center compares reported conditions with current zone coverage and escalates unresolved readiness gaps to the appropriate operational lead.
S050: Readiness status is reassessed after significant incidents, service interruptions, or changes to routes and access conditions.
S051: The Regional Dispatch Center handles incoming emergency calls through a controlled intake process that creates an incident record for coordination.
S052: Call Taker Mara is also known by the radio alias Larkspur.
S053: The Hospital Liaison Desk is also known by the coordination alias Kestrel.
S054: Call Taker Mara establishes the caller's location before collecting medical details.
S055: Call Taker Mara asks for the street address, municipality, and any building, floor, or entrance information needed to find the patient.
S056: Call Taker Mara confirms the location by repeating the address and checking it against the caller's description of nearby landmarks.
S057: Call Taker Mara asks whether the caller can provide a callback number in case the connection is lost.
S058: Call Taker Mara gathers the patient's age, level of consciousness, breathing status, and the main reason emergency help is needed.
S059: Call Taker Mara uses direct questions to distinguish observed symptoms from information reported by someone else.
S060: Call Taker Mara records the time symptoms began when the caller can provide a reliable estimate.
S061: Call Taker Mara notes access barriers such as locked entrances, restricted roads, or difficulty reaching the patient.
S062: Call Taker Mara produces the Caller Location Correction Slip when the caller's address needs documented clarification.
S063: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console checks entered location details against available address and map data.
S064: If the location does not resolve cleanly, Call Taker Mara asks focused follow-up questions and updates the incident record.
S065: Call Taker Mara remains engaged with the caller when further information could change the response priority or access plan.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
